reproduction_target: Saturation genome editing (SGE) readout pipeline for LMNA premature-termination-codon variants: paired-end read merging/error filtering (SeqPrep), perfect-match alignment to per-experiment gDNA/cDNA reference sets (Bowtie), per-variant read counting (Python), relative mRNA-expression calculation with variant filtering (Python), cross-experiment SNV-based normalization (R), transcriptional-activity and splicing-efficiency calculation from nascent-transcript libraries, NMD-efficiency calculation (Python + R normalization), plus three ancillary analyses: TOPMed allele-specific-expression (STAR/WASP + GATK ASEReadCounter + Ensembl VEP), reanalysis of published BRCA1/VHL SGE datasets, and NetStart 2.0 downstream in-frame AUG annotation. All wet-lab SGE construction, cell culture, editing, drug treatment, BrU labelling/IP and library preparation are out of computational-reproduction scope (counted in W).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the METHOD DETAILS sections 'Sequencing and read alignment', 'Calculation of mRNA expression levels and variant filtering', 'Calculation of transcriptional activity, splicing efficiency and variant filtering', 'Calculation of NMD efficiency and variant filtering', 'TOPMed Allele-specific expression analysis', 'Data analysis, statistical tests, and visualization', plus two analyses described only in Results (published BRCA1/VHL SGE reanalysis for Fig 4C-D; NetStart 2.0 annotation for Fig 4E). The two SeqPrep invocations (150-nt merge for variant calling; adapter-trimmed merge for indel frequencies) are folded into one step. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted. Stage-1 prose-only: repo landing page and README prose were read; script contents were NOT read line-by-line.

steps.label: Sequencing-error filtering / overlap merging of 150-nt paired-end NovaSeq reads with SeqPrep (https://github.com/jstjohn/SeqPrep); variant-calling pass '-m 150 -L 150 -o 150 -q 0', indel pass '-A GGTTTGGAGCGAGATTGATAAAGT -B CTGAGCTCTCTCACAGCCATTTAG -m 20 -L 20 -o 20 -q 0' (repo: SeqPrep.sh)

Alignment of merged 150-nt reads with Bowtie (Langmead et al. 2009), default parameters except '-v 0' (perfect matches only), against per-experiment gDNA/cDNA reference sets from Supplementary Table 3, plus a nascent-transcript reference containing the exon11-intron11 and exon11-exon12 boundaries; alternative references appended and realigned for SGE experiments 1, 4, 5, 6 (repo: Bowtie.sh)
Per-variant total read counting from Bowtie alignments ('Total counts for each variant were calculated with a Python script')

Relative mRNA-expression calculation with variant filtering (Python): cDNA count / gDNA count per variant, divided by the synonymous-context value; filters = SeqPrep-passing reads only, >=10 aligned reads in both gDNA and cDNA, variant present in both DMSO and SMG1i, replicate SD <= 0.2 (repo: Relative_mRNA_expression.sh)

Cross-experiment SNV-based normalization of mRNA expression with an R script: mean expression of each variant divided by the median expression of all SNV variants within the same SGE experiment (Fig 3A vs unnormalized Fig S4A)

Transcriptional-activity and splicing-efficiency calculation for exon-11 variants from nascent-transcript multiplex libraries: (spliced + unspliced) counts normalized to gDNA integration frequency and to the synonymous context; splicing efficiency = spliced/total normalized to synonymous context; filters = >1000 reads, SD < 0.2 (values in Supplementary Table 5)

NMD-efficiency calculation (Python): per-variant DMSO and SMG1i cDNA counts each divided by the synonymous-context count in the same library, then NMD efficiency = 1 - (DMSO/SMG1i); cross-experiment normalization by subtracting the median SNV NMD-efficiency per experiment (R script); same low-confidence filters as C4 (repo: Calculate_NMD_efficiency.sh; values in Supplementary Table 6)

TOPMed allele-specific-expression analysis: STAR aligner (Dobin et al. 2013) with WASP functionality (van de Geijn et al. 2015) for reference-bias mitigation, GATK ASEReadCounter version (v3), NMD efficiency = reference-allele count / total allele count sampled 100 times across carriers with median plotted; variant consequences and transcript mappings annotated on GRCh38 with Ensembl VEP v106 + dbNSFP and plugin suite

Reanalysis of published saturation-genome-editing datasets for BRCA1 (Findlay et al. 2018) and VHL (Buckley et al. 2024): RNA expression scores for synonymous vs PTC variants across the start-proximal region, used to delimit the NMD-inactive zone (Fig 4C-D)
Annotation of downstream in-frame start codons with NetStart 2.0 (Nielsen et al. 2025) for the seven-gene start-proximal NMD-dead-zone comparison (Fig 4E)

Statistical testing and visualization: n=3 biological replicates throughout; Wilcoxon rank-sum test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for stop-codon-identity comparisons (e.g. TGA vs TAA p=0.025, TGA vs TAG p=0.014); figure generation ('The exact code and packages used for these analyses can be found in this repository')

headline.static_readiness: 0/11 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Even under the most generous inference-inclusive reading, no step exceeds NI at stage 1, and only C8 reaches NI. The binding constraint is DATA, not code: the paper states 'All sequencing data have been deposited at GEO (xxx) and will be publicly available as of publication' - the accession is a literal unresolved placeholder '(xxx)', so no raw FASTQ, no aligned reads, and no per-variant count tables are obtainable today. Every core SGE step (C1-C7) therefore scores data=0 and is X regardless of how good the code is. The code side is comparatively strong: the repository https://github.com/jagannathan-lab/2025-cortazar_et_al is live (HTTP 200), public, and its README names the intended execution order (SeqPrep.sh and Bowtie.sh first, then Relative_mRNA_expression.sh and Calculate_NMD_efficiency.sh in any order); all four scripts resolve on the main branch. But the repo is a floating main branch with no tag, release or commit pin cited in the paper, and no environment.yml, requirements.txt, Dockerfile or renv.lock (all 404), and no version is stated anywhere for SeqPrep, Bowtie, Python, R or any R/Python package. Version therefore caps at 0 for C1-C7 and C9/C11. Once the GEO accession is filled in at publication this paper could plausibly move to RI on the core pipeline steps at a re-assessment, but it would still be blocked from R-star by the total absence of environment capture.
headline.coverage: 11 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus two Results-only analyses (C9, C10). 11 wet-lab steps counted (W, out of computational-reproduction scope): HDR library design and cloning, CRISPR gRNA design and cloning, cell culture, transfection, SMG1i/CHX treatment and BrU metabolic labelling, Br-RNA IP and RT-qPCR, in-vitro spike-in RNA synthesis, multiplex RT-PCR gel electrophoresis, multiplex library preparation from nascent transcripts, nucleic-acid sampling and sequencing-library production, Illumina NovaSeq paired-end sequencing. A 'Data and code availability' statement is present; a separate code-availability pointer is repeated in 'Data analysis, statistical tests, and visualization'.

gaps.where: All sequencing data underlying C1-C7 (gDNA, cDNA, HDR, negative-control and nascent-transcript libraries for all SGE experiments)
gaps.missing: The data-availability statement reads verbatim 'All sequencing data have been deposited at GEO (xxx) and will be publicly available as of publication.' The GEO accession is an unfilled placeholder '(xxx)' - there is no GSE identifier, no URL, and no reviewer token. No intermediate per-variant count tables are deposited either; only derived values (Supplementary Tables 4, 5, 6) and reference/template sequences (Supplementary Tables 1-3) are available.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the real GEO/SRA accession (and a reviewer access token pre-publication), and additionally deposit the per-variant gDNA/cDNA count matrices so the downstream normalization steps can be re-run without re-aligning terabyte-scale FASTQ.

gaps.where: Software environment for the entire analysis pipeline (C1-C7, C11)
gaps.missing: No conda environment, lockfile, container, or requirements file exists in the repository (environment.yml, requirements.txt, Dockerfile, renv.lock all return HTTP 404). No version is stated in the paper or the README for SeqPrep, Bowtie (major version 1 vs 2 not even disambiguated - only 'Bowtie (Langmead et al. 2009)'), Python, R, or any Python/R package. Exact pins exist only for the ancillary TOPMed step (Ensembl VEP v106, GATK ASEReadCounter v3, NetStart 2.0) and even there STAR is unversioned.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a pinned environment (conda-lock / pixi.lock / container digest) covering SeqPrep, Bowtie, Python + packages and R + packages, and record the resolved versions in the README.

gaps.missing: The repository is cited as a bare floating URL with no commit SHA, tag, release, or Zenodo DOI. There is no archival snapshot, so the code state corresponding to the preprint cannot be recovered if main moves. The README is 5 lines and documents run order only - no inputs, no outputs, no invocation examples, no license.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release, archive it to Zenodo for a DOI, and cite that DOI (or the commit SHA) in the paper. Expand the README with expected inputs/outputs per script.

gaps.where: C5, C6, C11 - R normalization scripts, transcriptional-activity/splicing-efficiency calculation, and figure/statistics code
gaps.missing: The paper claims 'All original code is available at the GitHub repository' and 'The exact code and packages used for these analyses can be found in this repository', but the README names only four shell scripts (SeqPrep.sh, Bowtie.sh, Relative_mRNA_expression.sh, Calculate_NMD_efficiency.sh). No R script, no splicing/transcriptional-activity script, and no figure/statistics script is named in the README prose. Whether they exist in the repo was not verified at stage 1 (prose-only).
gaps.how_to_close: Name every script in the README and map each Main/Supplementary figure to the script that produces it.

gaps.where: C2 Bowtie reference construction; C9 published-SGE reanalysis; C10 NetStart 2.0
gaps.missing: C2: which alternative reference sequences were appended for SGE experiments 1, 4, 5, 6 and how the two-alignment results were merged is described only narratively. C9: no method detail at all for the BRCA1/VHL reanalysis - source table, filtering, and the criterion used to draw the 'NMD dead zone' boundary (Fig 4C-E gray shading) are unstated. C10: NetStart 2.0 input transcript set and score threshold for calling a downstream in-frame AUG are unstated.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact reference-appending and merge rule, the download source plus filtering for the BRCA1/VHL datasets, the operational definition of the dead-zone boundary, and the NetStart score threshold.

gaps.missing: TOPMed cis-e/sQTL results are described as 'generated in a collaboration ... and distributed to TOPMed investigators' - a controlled-access, membership-gated resource with no dbGaP accession, study identifier, freeze number, or sample-set definition given. dbNSFP version is not stated. The '100 times sampled across individuals' resampling has no random seed.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the dbGaP accession and TOPMed freeze, state the dbNSFP release version, and fix/report the resampling seed.
